Hi Roger, thanks for the patch. Many parts of the platform spec support are implemented in a 'legacy' style. I've left comments inline about how I'd new APIs to be designed and implemented. Unfortunately it means that the library implementation isn't terribly consistent, but we can fix that over time.

Why 3 bytes here? The message has two 1-byte fields, `completionCode` and `transportProtocolType`. Beyond that, it's dependent on the latter. For MCTP, `eventReceiverAddress` should be 1 byte for the EID. NC-SI is a point-to-point protocol (with NC transmit governed by token-ring arbitration), so should have no need for any data here. Vendor-defined is obviously arbitrary. But the minimum size given NC-SI should be 2?
Acknowledged

Acknowledged

Please no more packed structs:

https://github.com/openbmc/libpldm/blob/9c57ef5d371cec85075c7524a34c77bb8d8d884b/docs/checklists/changes.md#L151-L152

While others here are marked packed, I've decided that's a legacy strategy that shouldn't be followed any further. I'm aiming for libpldm to provide an ergonomic C API, and packaged structs don't help that goal.

This decision has impacts on the implementation too.
Test fails without packed. Not sure why, need to investigate more. Feedback appreciated

I expect you're trying to cast the struct over the message buffer, which is what I'm asking you to avoid 😊

The idea of the encode/decode APIs they transform a standard C struct into a buffer, or a buffer into a standard C struct, without the mess that comes with `__attribute__((packed))`.

Note that we don't want to require that the caller supply us an exactly-sized buffer - this makes the APIs tricky to use in cases where messages are variable length. Instead, for `encode_*()` functions, we should use:

```
return pldm_msgbuf_complete_used(buf, *payload_length, payload_length);
```

This ensures the supplied buffer was at least big enough, but doesn't care if it was bigger than required, and provides the length consumed back to the caller.
